chapter_title: Concerning the Five Things that he constructed wit
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation


**
¶1:** Divine
 Wisdom,
 acting from
 the
 Lord
's living
 power
, formed five essential spiritual structures out
 of the channels
 through
 which interior
 life flows and the outermost rational
 forms remaining
 in what
 had been the
 dense corpor
eal states of evil and falsity —
 that
 is,
 from
 conquered
 natural
 substance
 now
 pressed
 into the
 service
 of heav
enly order
.

**¶2:** The
 first is the complete
 ground of doctrine that rests upon the
 sustaining power of the will —
 the foundation
 by
 which all
 spiritual weight
 is 
borne.

**¶3:**
 The second
 is the connecting framework of supporting
 truths —
 the ordered
 span
 of
 doctrine
 that stands vis
ibly before the will
 as
 the
 architecture
 through
 which its
 power
 is
 expressed.

**¶4:**
 The third is the constraining form imposed
 upon the hells:
 the fixed
 boundary by
 which states
 of evil and falsity are given
 determ
inate shape and
 prevented
 from expanding
 without
 limit.

**¶5:**
 The fourth is the full
 array of fundamental sustaining truths —
 holy
 in
 their
 completeness —
 established throughout
 the vast expanse of general natural
 knowledge, ordered across
 every domain of the spiritual world.


**¶6:** The fifth is
 the encomp
assing protection
 of doctrinal tru
ths on
 every side — the boundaries
 that enclose and guard the recipient forms
 in
 which
 good and truth are held
,
 so
 that nothing
 from
 the
 surrounding
 fals
ity may
 break
 in
 upon
 them.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The Living Spirit constructed five great things from veins and skull[s in the] hard [bodies].
The first is the disc that is placed upon [the sh]oulder of the Porter.
The se[con]d are the arches of [the] pillar that is before him.
[The th]ird is the [mou]ld of the fo[r]m for the gehennas.
The fourth are the [seven] pillars that he has erected in the great sea, in [the] seven parts of the universe.
The fifth are the four walls that surround the vessels.
